title: Spot the search mistake
idea: TOOL: common search bugs — missing found = False, using = vs ==, resetting the flag in the loop.

options: found was never created with found = False before the loop
exercises.explanation: If no item matches, found is never assigned, so printing it fails. Always start found = False before the loop.

exercises.prompt:
This always reports 'not found' even when the target is present. Why?

found = False
for n in nums:
    found = False
    if n == target:
        found = True
print(found)
options: found = False INSIDE the loop resets it every item, wiping an earlier match
exercises.explanation: Resetting found each pass erases a True from an earlier item. The found = False line belongs BEFORE the loop, once.
A single = assigns; comparing needs ==. 'if n == target:' is the correct test.

exercises.prompt: found = False must be set once, BEFORE the loop — not inside it.
exercises.explanation: Inside the loop it resets every item and forgets earlier matches. Before the loop, it sets the starting assumption once.

exercises.prompt:
Predict the output of this BUGGY code:

nums = [8]
found = False
for n in nums:
    found = False
    if n == target:
        found = True
print(found)

(target is 8)
exercises.explanation: Here it happens to work because 8 is the LAST (only) item — but on [8, 2] it would wrongly report False. The reset is still a bug.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a CORRECT search (flag set up once, before the loop).
exercises.explanation: Flag before the loop, loop over items, compare with ==, and set True on a match.

exercises.prompt: A search returns True when the target is absent. Most likely cause?
options: the if test is wrong — maybe comparing to the wrong value or using != by mistake
exercises.explanation: A wrong-way answer points at the comparison. Re-check that the if really tests n == target.

exercises.prompt: Using = instead of == in the search test is a real, common bug.
exercises.explanation: = assigns and == compares. Mixing them up is a classic slip; the search needs the comparison ==.

exercises.prompt: Why is 'set the flag once before the loop' the safe habit?
options: so one real match is remembered for the whole scan
exercises.explanation: Setting it once lets a single True survive to the end. Resetting inside the loop throws matches away.

exercises.prompt: Which is a correct membership search (not a filter)?
options: found = False ; loop ; if n == target: found = True
result = [] ; loop ; if n == target: result.append(n)
exercises.explanation: The found-flag loop answers yes/no. The second builds a list (filter); the third is a sum.
